analysis: This PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. Per the patch excerpt, the changes are (a) a new paragraph in the `darkbloom update` section saying that on a Mac running the `darkbloom cluster` service, the update command asks the cluster supervisor to restart into the installed release together with the other Mac after the pair drained, with a deferral exiting 1, and (b) a revised `[provider] auto_update` row mentioning the pair's coordinated update. The two supplied units are head-side text of the unchanged earlier sections (start, switch, logout, login, enroll, cache), which I read as surrounding context. I did not see the patched lines 1804-1810 or 2148 in the supplied head text, so I only have the patch excerpt for them. Doc-only, so no executable security control changes. The update description keeps the existing statement that bundle, binary and mlx.metallib hashes are verified before the binary is replaced. The coordinated restart is a new behavior in the code the doc cites (UpdateCommand.swift, ClusterServiceUpdateRequest, cluster supervisor), but that code is not supplied here. Questions for integration: whether the supervisor's restart request channel is authenticated or owner-only, whether the pair-wide restart honors the TB-003/T-043 watchdog and rollback assumptions, and whether the remote Mac's update is verified with the same hash checks. These are unverified contracts, not findings, because the documentation itself shows no regression. The login/logout, cache and drain text (A-008, T-041, T-053) is unchanged context and consistent with the threat model, and the cache text is consistent with T-041's operator-selected storage mitigations. No threat-model text needs updating from this diff alone, though a TB-003 or T-043 note on the cluster-coordinated update may be warranted once the code is reviewed.
